paras: Niki de Saint Phalle, one of the most famous artists of the 20th century, was a French-American born in 1930. She was brought up in a very conservative family, and yet, she rejected the staid, conservative values of her family to pursue a career in painting. __31__ Fortunately, painting offered her an effective therapy and a way to develop as an artist. Her famous “Nana” series gained universal praise. It is a testimony to the glory of women. __32__ Some of these sculptures are very big, “so that men would look small next to them.” Saint Phalle used vivid colors in these works and her female subjects dance cheerfully and merrily. __33__

The sculptures, however, have nothing to do with fortune telling. __35__
Saint Phalle passed away on May 21, 2002, in San Diego, California, at the age of 71. Her death meant the loss of a woman of diverse creative talents.
zhTranslation: 妮基・德・聖法勒是二十世紀最著名的藝術家之一，法裔美籍，一九三○年出生。她在非常保守的家庭長大，卻違抗家族那套古板保守的價值觀，走上繪畫這條路。__31__ 幸好，繪畫給了她有效的療癒，也給了她成為藝術家的路。她著名的「娜娜」系列廣受讚譽，那是女性榮光的見證。__32__ 這些雕塑有些非常巨大，「好讓男人站在旁邊顯得渺小」。聖法勒在這些作品裡用了鮮豔的色彩，作品中的女性歡快地舞動著。__33__
聖法勒以塔羅牌為靈感的雕塑公園「塔羅花園」，位於義大利的托斯卡尼省。__34__ 這座公園裡有塔羅牌上各種符號的雕塑。色彩鮮明的建築與雕塑相互組合，映照出二十二張塔羅大牌所代表的抽象意涵。不過，這些雕塑跟算命毫無關係。__35__
聖法勒於二○○二年五月二十一日在美國加州聖地牙哥過世，享年七十一歲。她的離世，代表世人失去了一位才華多元的女性創作者。

marks: Gladiators were combatants who fought against criminals, wild animals, and each other during the time of the Roman Empire.
paras: Gladiators were combatants who fought against criminals, wild animals, and each other during the time of the Roman Empire. They were armed with deadly weapons and in most cases fought till either one of them accepted defeat or was killed. __31__ Roman people enjoyed the sight of blood and violent death. They crowded into the arenas to watch gladiator games, just like we watch football, baseball, and tennis matches today.

__32__ Some were slaves bought from different lands under Roman control, and some were prisoners of war. Most of the others were volunteers, a group which once accounted for half of all gladiators. The majority of the gladiators were Thracians, Gauls, and Africans. These combatants were generally skilled fighters and were paid for their services. __33__ All of the fighters, both male and female, were well looked after by their owners and rewarded after winning fights.

Roman historians sometimes called gladiators hordearii, a Latin term which means “barley eaters” in English. __34__ Chemical analyses of the bones found in a gladiator graveyard indicated that the typical food eaten by gladiators was wheat, barley, and beans. __35__ In addition to a plant-heavy diet, gladiators drank plant ashes to fortify the body after physical exertion and to promote better bone healing. The diet that gladiators followed may be unconventional by modern athletic standards, but in the days of the Romans, this was the diet of heroes.
zhTranslation: 角鬥士是羅馬帝國時代的搏鬥者，對手是罪犯、野獸，也包括彼此。他們手持致命的武器，多數情況下要打到其中一方認輸或被殺死為止。__31__ 羅馬人喜歡看見血、看見激烈的死亡場面。他們擠進競技場觀賞角鬥比賽，就像我們今天看足球、棒球和網球比賽一樣。
__32__ 有些是從羅馬控制的各地買來的奴隸，有些是戰俘。其餘大多是自願加入的，這一群人一度占了所有角鬥士的一半。角鬥士多半是色雷斯人、高盧人和非洲人。這些搏鬥者一般都身手熟練，也因為出賽而領取報酬。__33__ 所有的鬥士，不分男女，都受到主人妥善照料，打贏之後還會得到獎賞。
羅馬史家有時稱角鬥士為 hordearii，這個拉丁文的意思是「吃大麥的人」。__34__ 在一處角鬥士墓地找到的骨頭經過化學分析，結果顯示角鬥士平常吃的是小麥、大麥和豆類。__35__ 除了以植物為主的飲食之外，角鬥士還會喝植物灰，用來在劇烈消耗體力之後強化身體，並幫助骨頭癒合得更好。以現代運動員的標準來看，角鬥士的這套飲食也許不太尋常，但在羅馬人的年代，這就是英雄的飲食。

marks: In ancient Egypt, the government was dominated by a single figure, the Pharaoh, who was considered the divine representative of gods on earth.
In the several-thousand-year span of Egyptian history, the general method of governing was quite consistent.
paras: Every civilization is built upon rules and regulations. In ancient Egypt, the government was dominated by a single figure, the Pharaoh, who was considered the divine representative of gods on earth. __31__ He was the supreme ruler and owned all of Egypt, the land and all the people who lived there.

__32__ There was a hierarchy of rulers and leaders below him who ran different aspects of the government. The primary leader under the Pharaoh was named the vizier. The vizier was the “right-hand man” of the Pharaoh and had a status equivalent to that of a prime minister. __33__ They ruled over an area of land called a nome. A nome was like a state or province.

Other officials that reported to the Pharaoh were the army commander, chief treasurer, and the minister of public works. Since government and religion were inseparable in ancient Egypt, many of the officials were also priests and holy men. This group had a special status above the rest of the citizens, forming a kind of nobility. __34__

In the several-thousand-year span of Egyptian history, the general method of governing was quite consistent. __35__ The consistency of this governing system is what allowed Egypt to remain a prominent country for such a long time.
zhTranslation: 每一個文明都建立在規則與制度之上。在古埃及，政府由單一人物主導，那就是法老，他被視為眾神在人間的神聖代表。__31__ 他是至高無上的統治者，擁有整個埃及——土地，以及住在那片土地上的所有人。
__32__ 他底下有一整套統治者與領導者的層級，各自負責政府的不同面向。法老之下最主要的領導者稱為 vizier（宰相）。宰相是法老的「左右手」，地位相當於今天的首相。__33__ 他們管轄一塊稱為 nome 的土地。nome 就像是一個州或一個省。
其他向法老負責的官員包括軍隊統帥、財政大臣和公共工程大臣。由於古埃及的政治與宗教密不可分，許多官員同時也是祭司和聖職人員。這一群人的地位高於其他百姓，形成某種貴族階層。__34__
在埃及長達數千年的歷史裡，統治的整體方式相當一致。__35__ 正是這套統治制度的穩定，讓埃及能夠長時間維持大國的地位。

marks: Ironically, Copernicus had dedicated his work to Pope Paul III.
paras: Copernicus, founder of modern astronomy, was born in 1473 to a well-to-do merchant family in Torun, Poland. He was sent off to attend university in Italy, studying mathematics and optics, and canon law. Returning from his studies abroad, Copernicus was appointed to an administrative position in the cathedral of Frauenburg. There he spent a sheltered and academic life for the rest of his days.

__31__ He made his observations from a tower situated on the protective wall around the cathedral. His observations were made with the “bare eyeball,” so to speak, as a hundred years were to pass before the invention of the telescope. In 1530, Copernicus completed his famous work De Revolutionibus, which later played a major role in changing the philosophical view of humankind’s place in the universe. __32__ Copernicus died in 1543 and was never to know what a stir his work would cause. In his book, he asserted that the Earth rotated on its axis once daily and traveled around the Sun once yearly. __33__ People then regarded the Earth as stationary, situated at the center of the universe, with the Sun and all the planets revolving around it. Copernicus’ theory challenged the long-held belief that God created the Heavens and the Earth, and could overturn the core values of the Catholic world. __34__ Other ministers quickly followed suit, saying of Copernicus, “This fool wants to turn the whole art of astronomy upside down.”

Ironically, Copernicus had dedicated his work to Pope Paul III. __35__ The Church ultimately banned De Revolutionibus, and the book remained on the list of forbidden reading material for nearly three centuries thereafter.
zhTranslation: 現代天文學的奠基者哥白尼，一四七三年出生於波蘭托倫一個家境富裕的商人家庭。他被送到義大利念大學，修習數學、光學和教會法（教會內部的法律）。結束國外的學業回來之後，哥白尼被派到弗勞恩堡的大教堂擔任行政職務。此後他就在那裡度過受到庇護、與學術為伍的餘生。

__31__ 他的觀測是在大教堂周圍防護牆上的一座塔樓進行的。可以說，他是用「肉眼」看的，因為望遠鏡要再過一百年才發明出來。一五三○年，哥白尼完成了他著名的《天體運行論》，這本書後來在改變人類看待自身在宇宙中位置的哲學觀上，扮演了重要的角色。__32__ 哥白尼於一五四三年過世，始終不知道他的著作會掀起多大的波瀾。他在書中主張，地球每天繞著地軸自轉一圈，每年繞太陽公轉一圈。__33__ 當時的人認為地球是靜止的，位在宇宙的中心，太陽和所有行星都繞著它轉。哥白尼的理論挑戰了長久以來「上帝創造天地」的信念，也可能顛覆天主教世界的核心價值。__34__ 其他教士很快跟進，說哥白尼「這個蠢材想把整個天文學徹底翻過來」。
諷刺的是，哥白尼把這部著作獻給了教宗保祿三世。__35__ 教會最終查禁了《天體運行論》，此後將近三個世紀，這本書一直留在禁書名單上。

paras: The causes of the French Revolution are complex and still widely debated among historians. However, many scholars agree that food played an important role in the socio-political upheaval. __31__

A main component in the French daily meal, bread was often tied up with the national identity. Studies show that the average 18th-century French worker spent half his daily wage on bread. In 1788 and 1789, however, when the grain crops failed two years in a row, the price of bread shot up to 88 percent of his earnings. __32__ The great majority of the French population was starving. Some even resorted to theft or prostitution to stay alive.

__33__ Started in the 15th century, this tax on salt consumption was applied particularly to the poor, while the nobility and the privileged were exempted. The high rate and unequal distribution of the tax provoked widespread illegal dealing in salt by smugglers, leading to skyrocketing salt prices.

However, the royal court at Versailles was isolated from and indifferent to the escalating crisis. The desperate population thus blamed the ruling class for the famine and economic disturbances. __34__ The results include the storming of the Bastille, a medieval fortress and prison in Paris, and the eventual beheading of King Louis XVI and his wife, Marie Antoinette.
__35__ Yet, the gabelle and the “bread question” remained among the most unsettling social and political issues throughout the Revolutionary and Napoleonic periods (1789-1815) and well beyond.

麵包是法國人日常飲食的主要部分，往往和民族認同綁在一起。研究顯示，十八世紀的法國工人平均要拿出半天的工資買麵包。然而在一七八八和一七八九年，穀物連續兩年歉收，麵包的價格飆漲到工人收入的百分之八十八。__32__ 絕大多數的法國人處於挨餓狀態。有些人甚至靠偷竊或賣身求生。
__33__ 這項對鹽課徵的消費稅始於十五世紀，特別針對窮人，貴族和特權階級則不必繳。稅率高又課得不公平，引發私鹽販子大規模的非法交易，鹽價因此一路飆升。
然而，凡爾賽的王室既與這場不斷惡化的危機隔絕，也對它漠不關心。走投無路的民眾於是把飢荒和經濟動盪都歸咎於統治階級。__34__ 後果包括攻陷巴士底獄——那是巴黎一座中世紀的堡壘兼監獄——以及路易十六和他的妻子瑪麗・安東妮最終被送上斷頭台。
__35__ 不過，鹽稅（gabelle）和「麵包問題」始終是革命時期與拿破崙時期（一七八九至一八一五年）以及其後很長一段時間裡，最令人不安的社會與政治議題之一。

A cockroach can grow back a missing limb, but the limb itself can’t generate a new cockroach. __33__ Bidirectional regeneration, on the other hand, refers to a situation in which splitting of an animal will result in separate fully functional animals.
__34__ Cut a hydra in half, and you’ll get two hydras. Cut it into four pieces, and you’ll get four.

__35__ A single one can be cut into hundreds of pieces and each will grow back into a whole in a week or so. 歷史：從十九世紀的勝家縫紉機到速食連鎖
優點：現成的營運模式、總部支援，還有品牌名氣

marks: The concept of the franchise dates back to the 19th century in the U.S.
There are many advantages to investing in a franchise.
Disadvantages include heavy start-up costs as well as ongoing royalty costs on the part of the franchisee.
paras: Starting a business on one’s own can be quite challenging and costly. To reduce the risks involved in starting a business from scratch, many people buy a franchise instead. __31__ Under the license, the individual acquires the right to use the big company’s brand name and agrees to sell its products.

The concept of the franchise dates back to the 19th century in the U.S. __32__ Then, in the 1930s, Howard Johnson restaurants skyrocketed in popularity, paving the way for restaurant chains and the subsequent franchises that would define the unprecedented rise of the American fast-food industry.

There are many advantages to investing in a franchise. One of the benefits is the ready-made business operation. __33__ Depending on the franchise, the franchisor company may offer support in training and financial planning. Some even provide assistance with approved suppliers. To new business owners, the most recognized advantage of a franchise is perhaps the well-established brand name of the franchisor such as that of McDonald’s. __34__

Disadvantages include heavy start-up costs as well as ongoing royalty costs on the part of the franchisee. To take the McDonald’s example further, the estimated minimum cost for a franchisee to start a McDonald’s is US$500,000. And it has to pay an annual fee equivalent to 12% of its sales to McDonald’s.
__35__ Other disadvantages include lack of territory control or creativity with one’s own business.
zhTranslation: 自己開一家公司相當有挑戰性，成本也高。為了降低從零開始創業的風險，許多人改為買下一個加盟權。__31__ 依照這張授權，個人取得使用那家大公司品牌名稱的權利，並同意銷售它的產品。
加盟這個概念可以追溯到十九世紀的美國。__32__ 後來在一九三○年代，Howard Johnson 餐廳人氣暴漲，替連鎖餐廳鋪了路，也帶出後來的加盟體系——美國速食業前所未有的興起，正是由這些加盟體系形塑出來的。
投資加盟有許多好處。其中之一是現成的營運模式。__33__ 依加盟品牌而異，加盟總部可能提供訓練和財務規劃方面的支援。有些甚至協助引介經過認可的供應商。對新的業主來說，加盟最廣為人知的好處，也許是總部那個早已建立起來的品牌名稱，例如麥當勞。__34__
缺點包括加盟主要負擔沉重的開辦成本，以及持續支付的權利金。再以麥當勞為例，加盟主要開一家麥當勞，估計最少要五十萬美元，而且每年還必須付給麥當勞相當於營業額百分之十二的費用。
__35__ 其他缺點包括無法掌控自己的營業區域，也無法在自己的生意上發揮創意。

marks: Since the early 1990s, the lithium-ion battery has been the most suitable battery for portable electronic equipment.
Lithium-ion batteries have nearly twice the energy density of traditional nickel cadmium batteries.
It should be noted, however, that manufacturers are constantly making improvements on lithium-ion batteries.
paras: Since the early 1990s, the lithium-ion battery has been the most suitable battery for portable electronic equipment. Today, they’re commonly used for cellphones, computers, tablets, digital cameras, and other devices.

Lithium-ion batteries have nearly twice the energy density of traditional nickel cadmium batteries. __31__ This feature has important implications for cellphones and computers, because it makes these items more portable for consumers. It also makes power tools easier to use and allows workers to use them for longer periods of time.

__32__ Lithium-ion batteries retain no “memory” of their power capacity from previous charging cycles. Thus they require no scheduled cycling and can be fully re-fueled to their maximum capacity during each charging cycle. Other rechargeable battery types, in contrast, retain information from previous charging cycles, which wastes valuable storage space. Over time, this makes these rechargeable batteries hold less of a charge.

__33__ It is fragile and requires a protection circuit to maintain safe operation. A high load could overheat the pack and safety might be jeopardized. __34__ After 2-3 years of use, the pack often becomes unserviceable due to a large voltage drop caused by high internal resistance.

It should be noted, however, that manufacturers are constantly making improvements on lithium-ion batteries. __35__ With such rapid progress, the use of lithium-ion batteries will certainly expand further.
zhTranslation: 自一九九○年代初期以來，鋰電池一直是最適合可攜式電子設備的電池。今天，手機、電腦、平板、數位相機和其他裝置普遍都用它。
鋰電池的能量密度將近傳統鎳鎘電池的兩倍。__31__ 這個特點對手機和電腦有重要意義，因為它讓這些東西對消費者來說更便於攜帶。它也讓電動工具更好用，工人可以連續使用更長的時間。
__32__ 鋰電池不會「記住」前幾次充電循環的電量。因此它們不需要按表操課地充放電，每一次充電都能充回最大容量。相對地，其他可充電電池會保留前幾次充電循環的資訊，白白占掉寶貴的儲存空間。久而久之，這會使這些可充電電池能存的電愈來愈少。
__33__ 它很脆弱，需要一組保護電路才能安全運作。負載過高可能使電池組過熱，安全就有疑慮。__34__ 使用二到三年之後，電池組往往因為內阻太高造成電壓大幅下降而不堪使用。
不過要注意的是，製造商持續在改良鋰電池。__35__ 進展如此快速，鋰電池的使用範圍必然會再擴大。

marks: Eccentrics are people who have an unusual or odd personality, set of beliefs, or behavior pattern.
Once considered socially unacceptable, eccentric people have been found to possess some positive characteristics.
Psychologists therefore suggest that we pay attention to those who do not conform.
paras: Eccentrics are people who have an unusual or odd personality, set of beliefs, or behavior pattern. They may or may not comprehend the standards for normal behavior in their culture. They simply don’t care about the society’s disapproval of their habits or beliefs.

Once considered socially unacceptable, eccentric people have been found to possess some positive characteristics. __31__ They often have more curiosity about the world and, in many cases, are contentedly obsessed by hobbies and interests. __32__ They live in a world of their own and do not worry about what others think of them. So they are usually less restricted and therefore more carefree in forming new ideas.

__33__ Statistics show they visit their doctors less—about once in eight to nine years, which is 20 times less than the average person. This could be partly due to their innate traits such as humor and happiness. __34__ This may explain why eccentrics are, on the whole, healthier.

Psychologists therefore suggest that we pay attention to those who do not conform. It could be our aunt who has been raising pet lizards. __35__ Their crazy hobby or strange sense of humor is what keeps them going. Eccentric people may seem odd, but they will likely live a happier and healthier life because they enjoy what they are doing. In fact, many of history’s most brilliant minds have displayed some unusual behaviors and habits.
zhTranslation: 怪咖是指個性、信念或行為模式異於常人的人。他們可能懂、也可能不懂自己文化裡對於正常行為的標準。他們就是不在乎社會不認同自己的習慣或信念。
過去人們認為怪咖不見容於社會，如今研究卻發現他們具有一些正面特質。__31__ 他們對世界往往更有好奇心，而且很多時候會心滿意足地沉迷於自己的嗜好和興趣。__32__ 他們活在自己的世界裡，不擔心別人怎麼看自己。所以他們通常比較不受拘束，在形成新想法時也就更加自在。
__33__ 統計顯示，他們看醫生的次數比較少——大約八到九年才看一次，比一般人少二十倍。這可能有一部分要歸因於他們天生的特質，例如幽默和快樂。__34__ 這或許可以解釋，為什麼怪咖整體來說比較健康。
因此心理學家建議，我們應該多注意那些不隨俗的人。那可能是我們那位養寵物蜥蜴的阿姨。__35__ 他們那些瘋狂的嗜好或古怪的幽默感，正是支撐他們走下去的東西。怪咖看起來也許古怪，但他們很可能過得更快樂、更健康，因為他們享受自己正在做的事。事實上，歷史上許多最聰明的頭腦都表現過一些不尋常的行為和習慣。

paras: In the Dutch colonial town later known as Albany, New York, there lived a baker, Van Amsterdam, who was as honest as he could be. He took great care to give his customers exactly what they paid for—not more and not less.

One Saint Nicholas Day morning, when the baker was just ready for business, the door of his shop flew open. __31__ She asked for a dozen of the baker’s Saint Nicholas cookies. Van Amsterdam counted out twelve cookies. But the woman insisted that a dozen is thirteen. Van Amsterdam was not a man to bear foolishness. He refused. The woman turned to go without the cookies but she stopped at the door, saying, “Van Amsterdam! However honest you may be, your heart is small and your fist is tight.” Then she was gone.
__32__ His bread rose too high or not at all. His pies were sour or too sweet. His cookies were burnt or doughy. His customers soon noticed the difference and slipped away.
A year passed. The baker grew poorer and poorer. Finally, on the day before Saint Nicholas Day, no customer came to his shop. __33__

That night, the baker had a dream. He saw Saint Nicholas pulling out gifts from his baskets for a crowd of happy children. No matter how many presents Nicholas handed out, there were always more to give. Then somehow, Saint Nicholas turned into the old woman with the long black shawl!
__34__ He suddenly realized that he always gave his customers exactly what they paid for, “But why not give more?”

The next morning, on Saint Nicholas Day, the baker rose early to make cookies. And to his surprise, the cookies were as fine as they could be. When he had just finished, the old woman appeared at his door again. She asked for a dozen of Van Amsterdam’s Saint Nicholas cookies. __35__
When people heard he counted thirteen as a dozen, he had more customers than ever and became wealthy. The practice then spread to other towns as a common custom.
zhTranslation: 在後來稱為紐約州奧本尼的那座荷蘭殖民小鎮上，住著一位名叫 Van Amsterdam 的麵包師傅，他誠實得不能再誠實。他非常用心，顧客付多少錢就給多少東西——不多也不少。
聖尼古拉節那天早上，麵包師傅才剛準備好要開門做生意，店門忽然被推開。__31__ 她要買一打師傅做的聖尼古拉餅乾。Van Amsterdam 數出十二塊餅乾。但那位婦人堅持一打是十三塊。Van Amsterdam 不是那種會容忍胡鬧的人。他拒絕了。婦人沒買餅乾就轉身要走，卻在門口停下，說：「Van Amsterdam！你再怎麼誠實，還是心胸狹小、出手小氣。」然後她就走了。
__32__ 他烤的麵包不是發過頭就是完全不發。派不是酸就是太甜。餅乾不是烤焦就是還沒熟。顧客很快就察覺不對勁，一個個溜走了。
一年過去了。師傅愈來愈窮。終於，在聖尼古拉節的前一天，他的店裡一個顧客也沒來。__33__
那天晚上，師傅做了一個夢。他看見聖尼古拉從籃子裡拿出禮物，發給一群開心的孩子。不管尼古拉發出多少禮物，籃子裡總是還有更多可以給。然後不知怎麼地，聖尼古拉變成了那位披著黑色長披肩的老婦人！
__34__ 他忽然明白，自己一直都是顧客付多少就給多少，「但為什麼不多給一點呢？」
隔天早上，聖尼古拉節當天，師傅一早起來做餅乾。令他意外的是，餅乾好得不能再好。他才剛做完，那位老婦人又出現在他門口。她要買一打 Van Amsterdam 的聖尼古拉餅乾。__35__

paras: Do you have trouble getting started in the morning? Do you have problems learning early in the day? If you do, you are not alone. __31__ They learn better at night than they do in the morning.

To investigate when cockroaches learn best, researchers at Vanderbilt University tested the insects for which odor (peppermint or vanilla) they preferred. Most cockroaches preferred the smell of vanilla to that of peppermint at all times. __32__ Therefore, the scientists trained the cockroaches to prefer the peppermint smell by rewarding the insects with a taste of sugar water when they approached a peppermint smell. __33__

When the cockroaches were trained at night, they remembered the new associations (peppermint = sugar water; vanilla = salt water) for up to 48 hours. However, if the cockroaches were trained in the morning, they quickly forgot which smell went with which water. __34__

So, cockroaches learn better at night than they do in the morning. __35__ Because of this, it is likely that information they gather at night will be more useful to them. These experiments provide some clues about the interactions between body rhythms, learning and memory.

為了研究蟑螂什麼時候學得最好，范德堡大學的研究人員測試這些昆蟲偏好哪一種氣味（薄荷或香草）。多數蟑螂在任何時間都比較喜歡香草味，不喜歡薄荷味。__32__ 因此，科學家訓練蟑螂改為偏好薄荷味：只要牠們靠近薄荷味，就給牠們嘗一口糖水當獎賞。__33__
蟑螂如果在夜間受訓，這些新的連結（薄荷＝糖水；香草＝鹽水）牠們可以記住長達四十八小時。但如果是在早上受訓，牠們很快就忘記哪一種氣味配哪一種水。__34__
所以，蟑螂晚上學東西的效果比早上好。__35__ 正因如此，牠們在夜間蒐集到的訊息，很可能對牠們比較有用。這些實驗為身體節律、學習與記憶之間的互動提供了一些線索。

When it was time to go to college, Whitney was quite nervous. She was going to be rooming with someone she didn’t know and living in a town 300 miles away from home. There wouldn’t be a single person she knew in town. __32__

The first week of classes, something happened that changed Whitney’s life forever. __33__ She told everyone where she came from and all of the other ordinary details that students share in such situations. The final question for each student to answer was, “what is your goal for this class?” Most of the students said that they would like to get a good grade, pass the class or something similar. __34__ She said that her goal was to make just one good friend.

While most of the students sat in silence, one student came to Whitney and held out her hand and introduced herself. She asked if they could be friends. The whole room was silent. All eyes focused on Whitney and the hand extended just in front of her. __35__
Whitney learned the power of asking for what she wanted and taking action on that day.
zhTranslation: 曾經有一段時間，Whitney 沒有什麼朋友。她有點害羞、有點內向。__31__ 然而整個高中時期，她都沒能交到好朋友，也沒找到能作伴的人。
該上大學的時候，Whitney 相當緊張。她要和一個不認識的人同住一間寢室，還要住在離家三百英里遠的城鎮。那裡不會有任何一個她認識的人。__32__
開學第一週，發生了一件事，永遠改變了 Whitney 的人生。__33__ 她告訴大家自己從哪裡來，以及學生在這種場合會說的其他一般細節。每個學生要回答的最後一個問題是：「你這門課的目標是什麼？」多數學生說他們想拿到好成績、想通過這門課，或類似的話。__34__ 她說，她的目標只是交到一個好朋友。
多數學生都靜靜坐著的時候，有一個學生走向 Whitney，伸出手來自我介紹。她問她們能不能做朋友。整間教室鴉雀無聲。所有的目光都集中在 Whitney 身上，以及那隻就伸在她面前的手。__35__
就在那一天，Whitney 學到了說出自己想要什麼、並且採取行動的力量。

paras: It is impossible to imagine Paris without its cafés. The city has some 12,000 cafés varying in size, grandeur, and significance. The cafés are like an extension of the French living room, a place to start and end the day, to gossip and debate.

__41__ The oldest café in Paris is Le Procope. It was opened in 1686 by Francesco Procopio dei Coltelli, the man who turned France into a coffee-drinking society. __42__ By the end of the 18th century, all of Paris was intoxicated with coffee and the city supported some 700 cafés. __43__ By the 1840s the number of cafés had grown to 3,000. The men who gathered in these cafés and set the theme of the times included journalists, playwrights and writers. Around the turn of the 20th century, the sidewalk cafés became the meeting halls for artists and literary figures.

__44__ The artists gathered at the café may not be as great as those of the past, but faces worth watching are just the same. __45__ You’ll see the old men in navy berets; ultra-thin, bronzed women with hair dyed bright orange; and schoolchildren sharing an afternoon chocolate with their mothers. The café in Paris has always been a place for seeing and being seen.
zhTranslation: 很難想像巴黎沒有咖啡館會是什麼樣子。這座城市大約有一萬兩千家咖啡館，大小、氣派程度與重要性各不相同。咖啡館就像法國人客廳的延伸，是一天的起點與終點，也是閒聊與辯論的地方。

__41__ 巴黎最老的咖啡館是 Le Procope，一六八六年由 Francesco Procopio dei Coltelli 開設，正是這個人讓法國變成一個喝咖啡的社會。__42__ 到十八世紀末，整個巴黎都為咖啡著迷，全城養得起大約七百家咖啡館。__43__ 到了一八四○年代，咖啡館的數量已成長到三千家。聚在這些咖啡館裡、為那個時代定調的人，包括記者、劇作家和作家。大約在二十世紀初，露天咖啡座成了藝術家與文人的聚會場所。
__44__ 聚在咖啡館的藝術家也許不如過去那些人偉大，但值得一看的面孔還是一樣多。__45__ 你會看見戴著深藍色貝雷帽的老人；瘦得不得了、皮膚曬成古銅色、頭髮染成亮橘色的女人；還有下午和媽媽分著喝一杯熱巧克力的學童。巴黎的咖啡館向來就是一個看人、也被人看的地方。

paras: Japan is dealing with a problem that’s just starting to sweep the world—an aging population combined with a shrinking work force. __41__ By so doing, it is hoped that Japan’s government will save its increasingly burdened pension (i.e., payment received after retirement) system from going bankrupt. In 2000, the Japanese could get a full pension from the government at 60. __42__ What’s more, premiums paid by workers every month are set to rise while payouts they get after retirement fall.

To help workers to cope with this, Japan passed a law last year that requires companies by 2013 to raise their retirement age from 60 to 65 or rehire their retired workers. __43__ In a country where forced layoffs are a last resort, large companies traditionally have relied on retirement to reduce payrolls. They were just about to enjoy a big cut in personnel costs because of the mass retirement of Japan’s baby boomers. __44__ Consequently, there was much opposition from corporations to the new retirement law. Early signs suggest that large corporations will hesitate in raising their retirement ages. __45__ Violators of the new law would face only “administrative guidance,” not penalties. Such resistance is hurting the effectiveness of the policies, which may thus prolong the aging problem.
zhTranslation: 日本正在處理一個才剛開始席捲全世界的問題——人口老化，同時勞動力萎縮。__41__ 藉此，日本政府希望能讓負擔日益沉重的年金制度（也就是退休後領取的給付）免於破產。二○○○年時，日本人六十歲就可以從政府那裡領到全額年金。__42__ 此外，勞工每月繳的保費將調升，退休後領到的給付則將減少。

為了幫勞工因應這件事，日本去年通過一項法律，要求企業在二○一三年前把退休年齡從六十歲提高到六十五歲，或者把退休員工再僱用回來。__43__ 在一個把強制裁員當成最後手段的國家，大企業傳統上都是靠退休來縮減人事。日本嬰兒潮世代大量退休，本來正要讓這些企業大幅節省人事成本。__44__ 因此，企業界對這項新的退休法規有很多反對聲音。早期跡象顯示，大企業對於調高退休年齡會有所遲疑。__45__ 違反新法者只會受到「行政指導」，不會有罰則。這樣的抵制正在削弱政策的效果，也可能因此拖長老化問題。

title: 出生序與智力（Birth Order and Intelligence）

options.A: There are definitely two sides to this issue.
options.B: Scores decreased as the family size increased and also with birth order.
options.C: An intelligence test was administered to over 350,000 Dutch males when they turned 19 years of age.
options.D: On the other side are Rutherford and Sewell, who studied more than 10,000 American high school graduates.
options.E: Since then, the theory has been elaborated and even extended to explain the positive effect of birth order on intelligence.

optionsZh.C: 一項智力測驗施測於三十五萬名以上的荷蘭男性，時間是他們滿十九歲的時候。
optionsZh.B: 分數隨著家庭人數增加而下降，也隨著出生序愈後面而下降。
optionsZh.E: 自那時起，這個理論持續被闡述，甚至被擴大用來解釋出生序對智力的正面效應。

paraLabels: 起點：早期荷蘭的研究發現出生序與智力測驗分數有關
交鋒開始：一派提出理論解釋，另一派檢驗後說效應根本不存在
分成兩邊：各自的主張和依據，到現在沒有共識
marks: One of the first studies was carried out in the Netherlands during the early 1970s.
paras: Many researchers have been interested in whether or not an individual’s birth order has an effect on intelligence. One of the first studies was carried out in the Netherlands during the early 1970s. __41__ The test was called the “Raven,” which is similar to the I.Q. test. The researchers found a strong relationship between the birth order of the test takers and their scores on the Raven test. __42__

In 1975, Zajonc and Markus developed the confluence theory to explain the negative effect of birth order on intelligence involving the data from the Dutch. __43__ However, Rutherford and Sewell in 1991 tested the theory and found no support for it. They concluded that birth order effects did not exist.

__44__ On one side there are Zajonc and Markus, who state that birth order effects may be explained solely by family size and the spacing of births. With short birth intervals, increasing order of birth will be associated with lower intelligence levels. But with long birth intervals, this pattern may be reversed. __45__ They show that the confluence model does not explain any relationship between birth order and intelligence that may exist in the American data. Up to date, there is no agreement between these opposing views. And such a debate may continue for years to come.
zhTranslation: 許多研究者一直很關心一個人的出生序會不會影響智力。最早的研究之一在一九七○年代初期於荷蘭進行。__41__ 那項測驗叫做「瑞文氏測驗」（Raven），性質與智力測驗相近。研究者發現，受測者的出生序與他們在瑞文氏測驗上的分數之間有很強的關聯。__42__
一九七五年，Zajonc 和 Markus 提出匯流理論，用荷蘭的那批資料來解釋出生序對智力的負面效應。__43__ 然而，Rutherford 和 Sewell 在一九九一年檢驗這個理論，並未找到支持它的證據。他們的結論是，出生序效應並不存在。
__44__ 一邊是 Zajonc 和 Markus，他們主張出生序效應完全可以用家庭人數和生育間隔來解釋。生育間隔短的時候，出生序愈後面，智力水準愈低；但生育間隔長的時候，這個模式可能反過來。__45__ 他們指出，匯流模型無法解釋美國資料中可能存在的任何出生序與智力的關聯。到目前為止，這兩派對立的看法仍沒有共識。這樣的爭論可能還會持續好些年。

paras: Starting around 4,000 B.C., traditional Chinese brush painting has developed continuously over a period of more than six thousand years. __41__

During the 1st century A.D., the art of painting religious murals gradually gained in prominence, with the introduction of Buddhism to China and the consequent building of temples. __42__ For example, paintings of historical characters and stories of everyday life became extremely popular. Besides historical figures, landscape painting was also common in Chinese brush painting. By the 4th century, this particular type of painting had already established itself as an independent form of expression. __43__ The blue-and-green landscape used bright blue, green and red pigments derived from minerals to create a richly decorative style; the ink-and-wash landscape relied on vivid brushwork and various intensity of ink to express the artist’s conception of nature as well as his own emotions. __44__ A great many artists in the 9th century painted in this genre and their subject matters included a rich variety of flowers, fruits, birds, insects, and fish.

Since the turn of the 20th century, painters have often mixed several colors on one brush or mixed their colors with black inks. __45__ Such techniques have been widely adopted and further developed in the contemporary period.

西元一世紀，隨著佛教傳入中國、寺廟隨之興建，宗教壁畫的藝術逐漸受到重視。__42__ 舉例來說，描繪歷史人物與日常生活故事的畫作變得非常盛行。除了歷史人物之外，山水畫在水墨畫中也很常見。到了四世紀，這一類畫作已經確立為一種獨立的表現形式。__43__ 青綠山水使用取自礦物的鮮明藍、綠與紅色顏料，形成裝飾性濃厚的風格；水墨山水則靠著生動的筆法和濃淡不一的墨色，表現畫家對自然的體會以及自身的情感。__44__ 九世紀有非常多畫家投入這個類別，題材涵蓋各式各樣的花卉、果實、飛鳥、昆蟲與魚。
二十世紀初以來，畫家常在同一枝筆上調和數種顏色，或把顏色與黑墨混合。__45__ 這些技法在當代已被廣泛採用，並進一步發展。

paras: Fiction is the name we use for stories that are make-believe, such as Harry Potter or Alice in the Wonderland. __41__ It can be so close to the truth that it seems as real as something that happened to you this morning. Or, fiction can be as fantastic as the most unbelievable fairy tale.

Not everything in a fictional story has to be made up. __42__ You, of course, are real, and the moon is real, and many of the things that you could describe, such as the stars, the wind, and the pull of gravity, would be real. __43__ It would be a trip you took in your imagination.

Nonfiction, on the other hand, is all about true things. __44__ Someone’s biography is nonfiction; so is your autobiography. So are articles in your local newspaper, and school reports on science. __45__ Imagine writing history about the 1989 San Francisco earthquake, or a report about a high school sports team. An old proverb says, “Truth is stranger than fiction.” Do you think that’s true?
zhTranslation: 我們把那些憑空編造的故事叫做虛構，例如《哈利波特》或《愛麗絲夢遊仙境》。__41__ 它可以貼近事實到彷彿就像今天早上發生在你身上的事一樣真實；也可以像最不可思議的童話那樣天馬行空。
虛構故事裡並不是每一件事都必須是編造的。__42__ 你當然是真的，月亮是真的，而你可能描述到的許多東西——例如星星、風、地心引力的拉力——也都是真的。__43__ 那會是一趟你在想像中完成的旅行。
另一方面，非虛構講的全是真實的事情。__44__ 某個人的傳記是非虛構，你的自傳也是。地方報紙上的文章是，學校的科學報告也是。__45__ 想想看，寫一篇關於一九八九年舊金山大地震的歷史，或是一篇關於高中運動隊伍的報導。有一句古老的諺語說：「真實比虛構更離奇。」你覺得這句話對嗎？

__32__ 在這段經濟衰退、人心不安的時期，全美各個年齡層的人都湧進自家園子種食物。這些數字很可觀。__33__ 而且估計有百分之二十一的種菜人，會像 Mayberry 一樣是頭一回下田。
問他們為什麼變得熱衷園藝，很多人提到經濟衰退帶來的寒意，以及種菜確實能帶來金錢上的回報。__34__ 另一些人則是擔心食物乾不乾淨、安不安全，認為在自家後院種植可以確保端上餐桌的都是好東西。__35__ 而隨著油價再度上漲，園藝工作成了一種既省錢又能紓壓的度假方式。在景氣低迷的時候，人們翻動土壤，省下伙食費，也換來好味道。
